summary: The prepared source already contains the solution for the reported MiniMax-H3 CLI error. Upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33365, merged as 101bb2327cdebf310d5261775f00eaef13a2e168, added bare local-path recognition for MiniMax-H3. In the prepared checkout, /mnt/models/MiniMax-H3 auto-selects the diffusion backend, resolves to MiniMaxH3Pipeline, and the exact reported arguments are all accepted with no remaining argv. No source correction was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Existing regression coverage for bare MiniMax-H3 local-path pipeline resolution, registered local diffusion detection, and automatic serve-backend dispatch; 3 tests passed.

Issue-specific offline probe: the exact reported argv selected the diffusion backend, left no unrecognized arguments, preserved all reported values, and resolved /mnt/models/MiniMax-H3 to MiniMaxH3Pipeline. Independent near-name pipeline boundaries MiniMax-H3.5, MiniMax-H3-4B, and not-MiniMax-H3 returned no non-diffusers pipeline.
Environment inventory only: one assigned AMD Instinct MI350X device was visible through Torch ROCm 7.2. This did not execute the MiniMax-H3 model or a GPU kernel.

gpu_execution.evidence: Only device inventory was queried. MiniMax-H3 weights were not available, and the original reproduction requests two GPUs while this task assigned one.

remaining_limitations: The original MiniMax-H3 checkpoint was not available, so model loading, semantic output, and memory/offload behavior were not tested.
The original two-GPU deployment was not reproduced because only one GPU was assigned.
The prepared environment is ROCm on an AMD Instinct MI350X, whereas the report used CUDA on RTX 3090 GPUs.
The conclusion is limited to the reported CLI parsing and automatic backend/pipeline routing defect.
